Use case: identity-preserve, precise-object-edit. Production animation in-between for a 2D game sprite. The FIRST input is the exact preceding key pose A, and SECOND input is the exact following key pose B, both already on the same 1024x1024 transparent canvas. Produce ONE newly drawn halfway pose at temporal t=0.5 between A and B. This is frame interpolation by drawing, NOT a new character design, NOT a crossfade, NOT a double exposure. Keep every hard armor detail, helmet shape, face crack, shading, icy blue palette, rendering texture, finger/claw anatomy, attachment points and strip count as unchanged as possible. The rigid helmet and chest must remain at exactly their existing canvas location and size (helmet centered near x=522,y=270, tip near y=321). No camera shift, no recentering, no zoom, no global floating offset. Only hands/forearms and the flowing cloth move to positions halfway between corresponding positions in the two references; neither overshoot nor extrapolate. Carefully match each existing cloth loop, fold and tip between both images; preserve connectivity and clean singly defined contours. Frozen highlights must remain stable to prevent flicker. Maintain all existing transparent space, full body, safe margin at least 64px each side. Do not broaden the silhouette beyond the two references. Output exactly one 1024x1024 RGBA transparent PNG with no background, ground shadow, lettering, grid, VFX, or added particles. Preserve transparent holes in the cloth.
Segment old00 to old01: hands extend outward slightly; cloth subtly opens. The output must be the very small halfway opening, still extremely close to old00.
